key_insight: Increasing free-stream turbulence systematically reshapes a moderate adverse-pressure-gradient boundary layer over an airfoil, making it more canonical while amplifying large-scale turbulent motions.
engineering_relevance: For aerodynamic design and testing, freestream turbulence cannot be treated as a minor disturbance because it strongly alters mean-flow development, skin friction, and turbulence levels in APG boundary layers.
method: Wind-tunnel tests on a NACA 0015 airfoil at 2° and 4° angle of attack to vary the adverse pressure gradient.
Hotwire anemometry measured boundary-layer profiles at x/c = 0.400–0.625 with β = 0.2–1.5.
Static grids raised freestream turbulence from 0.15% to 6% while keeping chord Reynolds number near 250,000.
evidence_signal: Across the measured cases, higher freestream turbulence reduced shape factor, increased skin-friction toward ZPG-like values, and amplified streamwise velocity variance with energetic structures at λx/δ ≈ 13.
watch_item: The results come from a moderate APG regime on one airfoil at fixed Reynolds number, so the trends may not transfer directly to stronger pressure gradients or different geometries.
paper_title: Effect of free-stream turbulence on a moderate adverse pressure gradient turbulent boundary layer developing over an airfoil
